image_description: A vintage two-tone (maroon and cream) Mercedes-Benz minibus parked on a paved surface at an outdoor car show. The vehicle features a distinctive rounded front end, a large windshield, and a side sliding door that is currently open with people standing nearby. A young boy walks in the foreground to the right, and part of a blue BMW is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle clearly exhibits a compact, high-roofed van/minibus silhouette distinct from full-size transit buses.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large split windshield is prominent, and multiple side windows are visible along the passenger cabin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant height relative to its width, and the entrance door is located at the front-mid section.
A large door panel is visible in an open position, consistent with a sliding mechanism typical of this vehicle class.
The short hood and grille placement indicate a front-engine layout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is completely occluded by the viewing angle; only the front three-quarters are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle features a two-tone maroon and cream livery, which fits the 'company livery' description, though it lacks specific route markings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible wheels are proportionate to a van/minibus and feature standard hubcaps/rims.
The window configuration and overall size are consistent with a vehicle designed for small group transport.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific make/model classification and ensure it aligns with the 'minibus' label rather than a standard van or full-size bus.
To verify spatial separation between the complex foreground subject (bus), the interacting humans, and the background buildings/cars.
To check for boundary bleeding or fusion artifacts around the open door frame and the contact points of the tires with the ground.
To assess overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle texture anomalies in the paintwork or chrome reflections.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of the open door mechanism and hinges
Geometric correctness of the wheel rims and tire contact patches
Boundary sharpness between the bus and the surrounding people/background
Reflection consistency on the chrome grille and headlights
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the interaction between the open door and the people standing next to it. AI often struggles with occlusion boundaries where human limbs meet vehicle interiors. Also, verify the symmetry of the front grille and headlights, as asymmetry is a common artifact in vehicle generation.
